concept: Arm C ceramic artist: Muted-on-Vivid, Diagonal Color Split, Color Blocking
negative_en: distorted fingers, low resolution, broken facial features, broken window geometry, fake-looking background, warped walls, impossible perspective, body distortion, 3D render look, cartoon style
prompt_en: Create a photographic gallery portrait of an adult ceramic artist arranging monumental glaze samples in a theatrical ceramics studio. Use the attached portrait as the appearance reference, retaining the recognizable face, long dark wavy hair, and natural skin texture. The artist wears a matte desaturated clay-gray coverall and stands behind a waist-high pale stone workbench, both feet planted on the floor. Her left palm rests flat on the workbench while her bent right arm extends forward, with the right fingertips touching the upper edge of one upright square ceramic slab seated securely in a shallow wooden groove. Three large geometric glaze samples stand separately on the bench, with broad opaque flat-color faces and crisp edges. Behind the artist, a huge planar backdrop is divided by a straight diagonal boundary rising from lower left to upper right: saturated cobalt blue occupies the upper-left field and saturated vermilion occupies the lower-right field. The muted gray clothing and subdued skin remain clearly separated from this vivid two-color environment. Compose a medium-wide frontal photograph that shows the entire diagonal division, both hands and the bench supports. The slab arrangement repeats large clearly bounded color blocks at a smaller scale, with controlled reflections preserving each flat hue. Use soft neutral frontal light on the face and a directional side light revealing the ceramic thickness. The visual priorities are the muted subject against the vivid environment, a legible diagonal color split, and distinct geometric color blocking; the ceramic artist remains the focal figure. Across the backdrop, two large colored regions occupy opposite sides of a diagonal boundary, and the directional division remains readable across the principal composition. These large bounded color fields organize the principal composition; each field retains photographic surface shading or depth cues. Keep the camera level at the artist's chest with enough floor visible beneath the bench to reveal both planted feet. Grazing light picks out the beveled slab edges and tiny glaze dimples within their otherwise broad color faces.
